entry.name: mc.retune~

arguments.name: standard pitch
arguments.description: Reference tuning in Hz, the default is 440 Hz.

attributes.name: correction_ambience_threshold
attributes.digest: Correction Ambience Threshold
attributes.description: Set the automatic bypass when the signal contains too much noise or background ambience (reverb). A value between 0.2 and 0.4 is usually a good starting point. Range: (-10...10).

attributes.name: correction_amount
attributes.digest: Correction Amount
attributes.description: Set the amount of pitch correction. 0 means no correction, 100 means full correction.

attributes.name: correction_bypass
attributes.digest: Correction Autobypass Threshold
attributes.description: Define the sibilance threshold at which the original signal is passed through unaffected. This bypass switch is required to make sure that sibilances in vocal recordings don’t sound too processed. A default setting of 100 is good.

attributes.name: correction_threshold
attributes.digest: Correction Threshold
attributes.description: Define the threshold at which the correction takes effect. For most applications this should be set to 0 as this will correct notes that are more that 0 cent off, wrt their ideal pitch. A setting of 10 will allow a pitch deviation of 10 cents in either direction before the correction takes effect.

attributes.name: enablednotes
attributes.digest: Enabled Notes
attributes.description: Either the keyword “all” or a list of notes in the range from 0 to the size of the current scale minus 1 (0 .. 11 in the case of a chromatic scale) determines which notes retune will quantize to. That list may also be sent in the form of a message (e.g. enablednotes 0 2 3 5 7 9 10 ).

attributes.name: pitchdetection
attributes.digest: Detect pitch
attributes.description: Returns the average pitch of the segment that is currently being analyzed. This can be used as a pitch detector. A return value of 0.0 means that no coherent pitch could be estimated. You should expect an output fundamental frequency in the range of 50 Hz to 1000 Hz. Please note that this feature is experimental and might produce unpredictable results. In particular, it might introduce octave errors for the measured pitch depending on the input signal. Output as a signal from the second outlet.

attributes.name: use_16bit
attributes.digest: Use 16-bit processing
attributes.description: Enable (1) or disable (0) 16-bit processing. Better CPU performance can be obtained by using 16-bit processing, and it is reccomended if you are using the object for pitch detection and not retuning.

attributes.name: varname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: windowsize
attributes.digest: Windowsize
attributes.description: Specifies the window size to be used for retuning calculations. The range is between 16 samples and the currently used signal vector size.

messages.name: defaulttuning
messages.description: Go back to the default 12 note chromatic tuning.

messages.name: flush
messages.description: Themessage is used in conjunction with sending MIDI notes and will re-enable all notes in a scale.

messages.name: getlatency
messages.description: Report the latency in samples introduced by the retune~ object out the rightmost outlet.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Enable/disable notes in scale via MIDI notes
messages.description: MIDI notes as list e.g. “60 100” and “60 0” to enable/disable notes in the current notelist. If the default 12 tone chromatic scale is active, sending the note C3 (60) will enable note 0 (60 modulo 12), which is C.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: Signal values in the second or third inlets are used to lock the retuned signal to a specific pitch (Hz) (inlet 2) or to de fine detune modulation (inlet 3) values (Cents).

outlets.description: The deviation in cents from the closest note detected.

outlets.digest: closest note and deviation in cents
outlets.description: A list composed of the closest note and the deviation in cents from the closest note detected.
